goal: The session transcript gains a dim HH:MM:SS timestamp on the first line of each block, a blank line between blocks when the speaker group changes, and a re-tuned style map where errors are never double-dimmed and agent text is visually dominant.

references: Spec FR-5: timestamp comes from the record's ts field, first line of each block only, continuation lines bare

Spec FR-6: blank line when the block group changes (agent prose / tool activity / operator / lifecycle); none between a tool call and its own indented result line, and consecutive tool_use blocks count as one tool-activity group
Spec FR-7: no error-class kind may map to dim header plus dim body; humanized lifecycle lines stay dim; agent text uses the default non-dim body style
constraints: Grouping logic may compare against the previous rendered entry only; no cross-record buffering beyond that, so the ~250ms incremental poll appends stay correct at the boundary between fetches
The first block on screen gets no leading blank line

Scroll-follow behavior and the scroll-up pause indicator must keep working; packages/flywheel/tests/test_session_screen.py::test_session_screen_scroll_up_pauses_follow_and_indicator_shows must stay green
Tests pinning the old packed layout or style map must be updated in the same commit, including packages/flywheel/tests/test_session_screen.py::test_session_screen_renders_all_message_classes

Add test coverage for the FR-5/FR-6/FR-7 acceptance: an agent block followed by a tool call shows exactly two timestamps and one separating blank line, a tool call and its result are not separated, and the style map contains no double-dimmed error kind
Commit with a Conventional Commits message before emitting intent=verify
non_goals: No iteration boundary markers or rules
No new keybindings, settings, or expand/collapse UI state
No changes to the dashboard screen or the flywheel_core.audit CLI
edge_cases: Incremental appends across poll boundaries: a new block arriving in a later fetch still gets its blank-line separator and timestamp relative to the last block of the previous fetch
Blocks rendering at the same wall-clock second still each get their own block-start timestamp
